issues: Historical assertion that first-born nativity can indicate the number of later siblings is not supported by independent birth records.
The author limits the first-born count to subsequent siblings; do not interpret it as measuring people born before the firstborn.
The fallback to a different native's chart when firstborn birth data are missing is acknowledged by the source and must not be erased.
Whether there are siblings, their described condition, and familial amity/concord are three different outcomes, not one composite score.
No birth time accuracy, sample, non-astrology family-size baseline, fertility-control variables, age cohorts or blinded tests appear.
The unnumbered introduction is not the next printed chapter CXVIII; its separate numbered sibling source begins lower in PDF598.
No actual person's siblings, relationship quality, health, fertility or genealogy can be inferred from this historical text.
Source images and selective anchors are preserved; a complete diplomatic transcription and scientific assessment remain open.
